stem: Meera's mother keeps a block of jaggery near the hot stove, and after some time it starts turning soft and syrupy at its melting point. Which statement best explains why heating a solid like jaggery or ice can make it melt, and why the melting point is used to identify this change?

options.text: Heating pushes the particles closer together until they stop moving, and the melting point is the temperature at which particles stop vibrating.

Heating makes the particles vibrate more vigorously until they can leave their fixed positions, so the solid becomes liquid; the melting point is the specific temperature (at atmospheric pressure) at which this change begins, so it can be used to identify it.
Heating turns the solid particles into gas particles straight away, and the melting point is the temperature at which the solid evaporates.
Heating changes the particles into a different substance, and the melting point is just a number chosen from a table for each material.

teacher.key_rationale: Heating increases particle vibration until particles can leave their fixed positions, producing a liquid; the melting point is the defined temperature at atmospheric pressure where solid becomes liquid, hence B. Options A (particles stop moving), C (direct gas change), and D (new substance / arbitrary number) are all incorrect particle-model descriptions.
